newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Russian U.N. envoy's car ticketed 3 times in a day.
newsitem.headline: Russian U.N. envoy's car ticketed 3 times in a day.

text.p: Russian U.N. ambassador Sergei Lavrov's car was ticketed three times on Monday while the driver was inside the vehicle, waiting to take the envoy to appointments, the Russian mission said on Tuesday.

In a note of complaint to the United States' U.N. mission, it said this practice created "artificial obstacles" to normal functioning and asked for "appropriate measures to be taken to avoid repetition of such incidents in the future."
Lavrov and his Belarus counterpart, Alyaksandr Sychou, are already at loggerheads with New York city authorities over a recent clash between two of their diplomats and two policemen.
Each side accused the other of resorting to violence after the police said the two diplomats had parked near a fire hydrant and were preparing to drive away while intoxicated.
City authorities also complained that the two U.N. missions owed tens of thousands of dollars in unpaid traffic fines. Diplomats are immune from prosecution.

In its latest note, Lavrov's mission said his car was ticketed "while it departed the mission's garage and was parked with a driver inside it in front of the mission's entrance," waiting to take the ambassador to a noon appointment.

"The same situation was repeated later on the same day, at 1:07 P.M., when the permanent representative was leaving for a luncheon and at 4:18 P.M., when he was leaving for another function, with two more parking violation tickets being issued to his car while the driver was waiting inside it."
The policeman issuing the third ticket "attempted to open the driver's door of the car," it added.
